kill_fact: The catalyst has FIRED, it was never sized to move this security, and the recorded floor is already broken. Verified against primary sources: Uber's own investor-relations announcement of 16 July 2026 confirms a voluntary cash takeover offer for Delivery Hero at EUR 41.50 per share, with Prosus having given an irrevocable undertaking to tender its ~17% residual stake, taking Uber to ~53% of the economics; closing is expected in the SECOND HALF OF 2027, conditional on BaFin approving the offer document and on merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances. Prosus's own 16 July 2026 release confirms the 16.8% residual and states Uber's offer is 'a fair price and effective way to comply with its commitments to the European Commission.' Size test: Delivery Hero market cap EUR 11.51bn at EUR 37.90 implies ~303.7m shares, so 16.8% is ~51.0m shares. The UNEARNED spread is 51.0m x (41.50 - 37.90) = EUR 184m; spread across Prosus's 2,111.8m shares that is EUR 0.087 per Prosus share - 0.23% of the EUR 37.85 price, more than a year out, with regulatory conditions attached. There is no event-driven asymmetry left. The defined-risk premise fails outright as well: the board's recorded downside floor of 37.365 has been traded through - PRX.AS printed a 37.27 intraday low and a 36.17 52-week low within the past week - and nothing contractual sits beneath it. There is no tender for Prosus shares, no deal price, no net cash (net debt USD 6.8bn). What sets the price is Tencent, marked at USD 113.8bn on Prosus's own NAV page (~74% of gross portfolio value), trading at HK$443 versus a HK$683 52-week high and below both its 50-day (HK$449.0) and 200-day (HK$538.5) averages. That is uncapped Chinese-internet beta wearing a special-situation label. The moderator's own conclusion - pass in the event-driven book, hand it to the value book - survives the attack: the ASSET VALUE is real and verified, the CATALYST is dead.
corrections: 1) MATERIAL - the recorded downside_floor of 37.365 is not stale, it is BROKEN (37.27 intraday, 36.17 52-week low), and the risk_reward of 2.76 computed from it is void. The file's own downside_floor field (32.0) is a modelled mark-to-market value, not a floor; it must not be carried in a floor-shaped field without that label, because nothing in this security obliges anyone to pay any number. 2) MATERIAL - share count / per-share denominator. Prosus's own disclosure states 2,111.8m shares outstanding (17 July 2026); the buyback shrinks it continuously. Per-share figures computed on any larger count are stale. On the correct count the residual Delivery Hero holding is ~EUR 0.92-1.00 per Prosus share (Prosus marks it at USD 2.2bn in the 24 July 2026 NAV, i.e. ~EUR 0.92), and the unearned spread is EUR 0.087, not 0.09-plus. Directionally identical, but the dossier should cite the company mark rather than the offer-price mark. 3) MATERIAL - the sop_bear mislabels its own adverse assumption. It marks Tencent down ~13% to 'the high HK$300s' and calls that 'a retest of levels within this drawdown.' Tencent's 52-week LOW is HK$411, so the high HK$300s is a FRESH 52-week low, not a retest. The EUR 32 bear value therefore requires a worse move than the file claims; the honest first waypoint is the EUR 36.17 low. 4) MINOR - omitted deal condition. Uber's 16 July 2026 release discloses an antitrust remedy the dossier's condition list misses: Delivery Hero will sell businesses in 14 overlap markets to SSW Partners for ~USD 1.6bn, and Uber has committed to no Domination and Profit Transfer Agreement for three years. Immaterial at EUR 0.09 per Prosus share, but it is an added execution/clearance dependency and belongs in the list. 5) MINOR - extension date. The dossier dates the EC extension to 2 June 2026 on a Naspers request of 25 May 2026; reporting places the Commission's confirmation on 29 May 2026, with 2 June the Bloomberg publication date. The deadline itself - 11 October 2026 - is confirmed. 6) CONFIRMED AS STATED - no Commission statement was found accepting a transaction completing in H2 2027 as satisfying the 11 October 2026 obligation; that remains genuinely open, and the dossier's reading (a negative answer forces a small residual placement, not a re-rating) is sound at ~EUR 1.00 per share of exposure. MLex reporting indicates the Commission viewed Uber's stake-building and prospective bid as justifying the delay. 7) CONFIRMED - the SoP stack ties exactly to Prosus's published 24 July 2026 NAV: gross USD 153.9bn, net debt USD 6.8bn, NAV USD 147.2bn, EUR 61.3 per share, Tencent USD 113.8bn, other listed USD 7.3bn (Delivery Hero 2.2, Meituan 2.1, Swiggy 1.5, Meesho 1.0), unlisted USD 32.8bn (Europe 15.9, LatAm 8.5, India 4.7, other 3.7). The target is real, not fantasy: at EUR 37.85 the discount to stated NAV is 38.3% and the buyer pays 0.80x the marked Tencent stake alone. The kill is on the CATALYST and the FLOOR, not on the asset value.
evidence: Uber Technologies investor relations, 'Uber Announces Acquisition Offer for Delivery Hero', 16 July 2026 (investor.uber.com): EUR 41.50 per share cash, ~USD 14.8bn equity value; Prosus irrevocably committed to tender its ~17% stake taking Uber to ~53% economic interest; minimum acceptance 50% plus one share inclusive of Uber-held shares; BaFin must approve the offer document before publication; subject to merger control and financial regulatory clearances; closing expected SECOND HALF OF 2027; Delivery Hero to sell 14 overlap markets to SSW Partners for ~USD 1.6bn; Uber committed to no Domination and Profit Transfer Agreement for three years.

Prosus N.V. announcement, 'Prosus gives irrevocable undertaking to sell residual stake in Delivery Hero to Uber', 16 July 2026 (prosus.com): confirms the 16.8% residual, the EUR 41.50 price, that Prosus 'committed to significantly reduce its 26.5% shareholding in Delivery Hero' under the EU clearance of the Just Eat Takeaway.com acquisition, and that Uber's offer 'represents a fair price and effective way to comply with its commitments to the European Commission'; also warns 'there is no certainty that the Offer will be implemented.'

Prosus N.V. investor relations, Net Asset Value page, as of 24 July 2026 (prosus.com/investors/investing-in-prosus/net-asset-value): gross portfolio USD 153.9bn, net debt USD 6.8bn, NAV USD 147.2bn, NAV per share EUR 61.3, shares outstanding 2,111.8m (17 July 2026); Tencent USD 113.8bn (~74% of gross), Delivery Hero marked USD 2.2bn, other listed USD 7.3bn total, unlisted USD 32.8bn.

European Commission divestment-commitment extension to 11 OCTOBER 2026, confirmed 29 May 2026 on Naspers's request (Bloomberg, 2 June 2026, 'Prosus Gets Until Oct. 11 for Delivery Hero Sale After Uber Bid'; MLex: Commission saw Uber's stake-building and possible bid as justifying the delay). Absent the extension Prosus would have had to unwind by mid-August 2026.
